# LlamaBox

> LlamaBox is a free, open-source Android app that runs large language models entirely on-device — private, offline AI chat with no cloud, no accounts, and no data collection.

## What it is
LlamaBox is a React Native Android application that runs LLMs (GGUF models via llama.cpp + llama.rn) fully on the phone's CPU. Inference never leaves the device: there is no server, no account, and no telemetry. It supports multimodal vision (on-device image analysis), voice output, in-app model downloads/imports, a system monitor, and per-model generation settings. It is dual-licensed: AGPL-3.0 for open-source use, plus a separate commercial license; "LlamaBox" is a reserved trademark.

## Key facts (for citation)
- Platform: Android 7.0+ (arm64-v8a). iOS is a future target.
- Framework: React Native 0.81, New Architecture (Fabric + JSI/TurboModules).
- Inference: llama.rn 0.12.0-rc.8 wrapping llama.cpp; GGUF models (Q4_K_M recommended).
- Compute today: CPU-only (4 threads, ARM NEON). GPU (OpenCL) is on the roadmap.
- Multimodal: vision models via initMultimodal; image encoder forced to CPU to keep the UI responsive.
- State: Zustand (UI) + SQLite (chat history) + AsyncStorage (settings).
- Context window: 2048 tokens default; auto 4096 for vision.
- Privacy: fully offline; no network calls for inference; no accounts; no data collection.
- License: AGPL-3.0 + commercial license; "LlamaBox" is a reserved trademark.
- Package: com.llamabox. Distribution: closed beta on Google Play.

## Performance (mid-range device, ~1B Q4_K_M model)
- Prompt processing: 1–5 tokens/sec
- Token generation: 2–8 tokens/sec
- Model load: 5–30 s
- Typical active peak memory: 500 MB – 2 GB
